title: Naturality of canonical abelian Čech comparison maps
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $U_i$ an open cover, $f:F\to G$ a morphism of abelian sheaves [def-sc-topological-abelian-cohomology], and $q\geq0$. If $c:\check H^q(U,F)\to H^q(X,F)$ and $d:\check H^q(U,G)\to H^q(X,G)$ satisfy IsAbelianCechComparison [def-pc-abelian-cech-comparison-construction], then $d\circ\check H^q(f)=H^q(f)\circ c$. This does not assert existence of comparisons or any boundary law.

source.place: Lemma 20.11.2, omitted coefficient-functoriality verification; Tag 01FD, augmented comparison squares

proof.text: Choose resolutions and a comparison lift of f. Naturality of restriction and the resolution lifting equation give commuting alpha and beta squares on cochain complexes. Apply homology.

Represent the comparison output by extMk; the constant-sheaf adjunction supplies its section cycle. Under the lift, extMk_comp_mk0 identifies the image cocycle with H(f) of that class. Apply both canonical comparison equations to these representatives.
The augmentation squares give equality after H(alpha on G) and the canonical section/Ext identification. Cancel the invertible maps and use extensionality.

lean.statement:
theorem abelianCechComparison_naturality
    {X : Scheme.{u}} {ι : Type u} (U : ι → X.Opens) (hcover : iSup U = ⊤)
    {F G : Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) AddCommGrpCat.{u}} (f : F ⟶ G)
    (q : ℕ)
    (c : (TopCat.Sheaf.cechCohomologyFunctor U q).obj F ⟶
      (Sheaf.functorH (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) q).obj F)
    (d : (TopCat.Sheaf.cechCohomologyFunctor U q).obj G ⟶
      (Sheaf.functorH (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) q).obj G)
    (hc : IsAbelianCechComparison U F q c) (hd : IsAbelianCechComparison U G q d) :
    (TopCat.Sheaf.cechCohomologyFunctor U q).map f ≫ d =
      c ≫ (Sheaf.functorH (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) q).map f
